absence is not a negative finding
normalization and learning happen under separate governed stages

pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fresh Stage Research re-entry for roadmap stage **Native Host v1 — Rust** after the CAP Core v1 boundary work.

This PR is **research/architecture only**. It adds no Rust toolchain, binary, public tool, local-execution grant, process launcher, PTY implementation or sandbox.

### Sequencing lock

```text
#159 -> #165 -> #166 -> #167 -> #168 -> #169 -> Native Host v1
```

This branch is stacked on #169 only to research the intended post-Core boundary. **Do not merge it into the current #169 base while #169 still needs exact-head acceptance**, because that would move #169's head. Refresh against the accepted/frozen Core before production implementation.

## Stage Research decision

```text
NATIVE_HOST_V1_RESEARCH_DECISION_V1
stage_decision=NARROW
implementation_language=RUST
implementation_authority=POST_CORE_FREEZE_ONLY
first_slice=WINDOWS_PROCESS_LIFECYCLE
ipc=SHORT_LIVED_LENGTH_FRAMED_STDIO
host_durable_state=NONE
pty=FOLLOWUP_SLICE_AFTER_PROCESS_SUBSTRATE
sandbox=SEPARATE_SECURITY_REENTRY
public_tool_change=NO
```

The merged #132 decision was correctly `DEFER / future_native_language=UNRESOLVED` on 2026-08-28. The stage question has changed: #168/#169 establish the Core adapter boundary and ROADMAP now explicitly selects Rust for the narrow post-Core native host. This re-entry does **not** reopen a broad "rewrite CAP in Rust" question.

## Stage goal

```text
ordinary ChatGPT
 -> CAP semantic capability
 -> CAP Core
      authorization / grants
      WorkingState / attempts / reconciliation
      Verification Kernel / Finish Gate
 -> capability-specific adapter
 -> Rust Native Host v1
      process tree / native handles / Job Objects
      bounded launch / cancellation / cleanup receipts
 -> operating system
```

The host executes an **already-authorized bounded operation** and returns evidence. It never plans, grants/renews authority, owns WorkingState, decides project PASS or task DONE.

## Current project baseline and lineage

| Role | Prior owner/source | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| General planning | ordinary ChatGPT | KEEP |
| Capability authorization | project CAP Core | KEEP |
| WorkingState / reconciliation | project Core | KEEP |
| Verification / Finish Gate | project Kernel / Finish Gate | KEEP |
| Agent-host source reference | Codex reference-only | KEEP |
| Native systems execution | no canonical baseline role | NEW / SELECTED_NARROW |
| historical Rust-first CAP runtime | `chat/rust-relay-server` | REJECT as architecture; ADAPT selected low-level mechanics only |

Historical project source inspected at `BogdanAIP/chat-agent-platform@347e798fcef1c7a6ed7242553ea9de2f444366db`:

- `reaper.rs` has useful bounded spawn/kill/reap patterns but only process-local `Child::kill`, not the new Job/tree boundary;
- `job.rs` owns durable job/idempotency state that would now duplicate Core WorkingState/attempt ownership;
- `transport/protocol.rs` is HTTP relay/cache and is the wrong boundary for private local native IPC.

Therefore the old Rust-first tree is reference material, not a branch to revive.

## Architecture primitives and adjacent domains

| Primitive | Direct engineering domain | Guarantee sought | Boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| per-operation host lifetime | OS process lifecycle / supervision | one native owner and one crash domain per attempt | no persistent service/session semantics |
| length-framed anonymous-pipe IPC | local IPC / protocol framing | bounded unambiguous message boundaries without a discoverable endpoint | transport receipt is not effect success |
| one-active-attempt host state machine | concurrency control | duplicate/concurrent Begin cannot cause a second spawn | memory-only; no durable host ledger |
| Job Object + suspended launch | Windows process containment | target cannot run before required tree containment is established | assignment failure is fail-closed |
| native handle ownership + inherited-handle allowlist | Windows object identity / least privilege | no PID-only kill authority and no accidental capability-handle leak | PID remains receipt data |
| Core-owned UNKNOWN/reconciliation | side-effect consistency / controller reconciliation | no blind retry after lost acknowledgement | WorkingState remains the sole durable owner |
| exact compiler/binary provenance | software supply chain | qualification binds exact executed host bytes/toolchain | no floating toolchain acceptance |

ConPTY and sandboxing are researched as adjacent future mechanisms but are outside the first implementation slice; adding them later is a stage sub-entry because they introduce terminal-input and security primitives.

### 1. One short-lived host per operation

First slice is **not a daemon**. One host process owns at most one active native operation. This removes daemon discovery, ACL/auth, reconnect, multiplexing and durable host-session state.

### 2. Private framed stdio

Selected transport is parent-created anonymous stdin/stdout pipes with a bounded length frame (`u32` length + UTF-8 JSON), explicit `protocol_version`, strict message enums and per-field limits. Stdout is protocol-only; diagnostics are stderr.

No TCP/HTTP listener, named-pipe service, port discovery or public RPC endpoint is introduced.

Initial correlation fields are `host_instance_id`, `request_id`, `logical_operation_id`, `attempt_id`, `authorization_ref`. The host treats authorization_ref only as correlation evidence; it cannot refresh or widen it.

The execution payload is typed `executable + argv + cwd + bounded_env`, never a Chat-facing `run_anything(command)` or raw shell string.

### 3. No host-side durable dedup ledger

The narrower lifecycle closes the #132 open question without SQLite/WAL/queue state:

- host accepts only one active Begin;
- duplicate/concurrent Begin in the same host is rejected before a second spawn;
- once delivery may have begun, missing terminal acknowledgement is ambiguous;
- a restarted host never auto-replays the unresolved attempt;
- CAP WorkingState remains the sole durable owner of `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` and reconciliation;
- another physical attempt requires fresh `CONFIRMED_NOT_APPLIED` plus normal grant/LoopGuard/budget checks.

Required observable invariant remains: **at most one physical spawn for an authorized attempt before reconciliation**.

### 4. Windows containment ordering

Selected first-slice process path:

```text
create/configure Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE
 -> create target suspended
 -> assign target to Job
 -> assignment succeeds
 -> resume target
```

No breakaway flag and **no compatibility fallback that resumes an uncontained consequence-bearing process**. Job/native process handles are the ownership identity; PID is receipt data only.

Handle inheritance must be explicit/allowlisted so protocol pipes, Job handles and unrelated resources do not leak into the child tree.

Parent protocol EOF is owner loss: terminate the active Job/tree, close/reap handles and exit.

### 5. Cancellation / completion

Safety cancellation is whole-Job termination, not generic Ctrl+C. Windows console control events are process-group/console constrained; graceful interrupt may later exist as best-effort behavior but cannot be the cleanup invariant.

Root-process exit is not tree completion. The host retains the Job and observes Job active-process state so descendants cannot be silently left running.

### 6. Bounded non-lossy output

Child stdout/stderr are bytes, not trusted text and not permission. The host must chunk/encode them into bounded protocol events without a lossy internal broadcast queue. Backpressure is allowed; silent dropping is not.

Each operation carries an authorized output budget. If the budget is exceeded or the protocol consumer cannot be maintained, terminate/fail the operation explicitly and report truncation/overflow rather than returning a normal-looking success with missing evidence.

### 7. Toolchain / binary provenance

Production implementation must pin an exact reviewed compiler and Cargo.lock. At research time Rust 1.98.1 is current; it is itself a patch fixing a 1.98.0 rustc vtable miscompilation, so a floating `stable` channel is insufficient release evidence.

Current `windows-sys` is the preferred thin Win32 binding candidate behind one audited platform module; actual versions are re-resolved at implementation time after Core freeze.

## Problem evidence

1. Native process ownership is distinct from PID/process-object convenience APIs.
2. Containment ordering matters: assignment after a process is already running leaves a pre-assignment window.
3. Broad inherited handles can leak files/sockets/tokens; Windows supports exact inherited-handle lists.
4. Root exit does not prove descendant-tree exit.
5. Transport ACK is not effect success; CAP already has UNKNOWN/reconciliation semantics that must remain authoritative.
6. Python/Node/PowerShell are not being replaced because they are 'bad'; the new role is only the low-level lifecycle seam after Core freeze.

## Solution evidence — engineering domain

Primary Windows sources researched:

- Job Objects — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/procthread/job-objects
- AssignProcessToJobObject — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/jobapi2/nf-jobapi2-assignprocesstojobobject
- Creating processes / handle inheritance — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/procthread/creating-processes
- Handle inheritance — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/procthread/inheritance
- CreatePseudoConsole — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/console/createpseudoconsole
- GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/console/generateconsolectrlevent
- Job accounting / ActiveProcesses — https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/winnt/ns-winnt-jobobject_basic_accounting_information

Relevant guarantees: Job Objects manage process groups as a unit; `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` kills associated processes on final Job-handle close; children normally inherit Job membership; nested Job assignment can fail and must be handled; STARTUPINFOEX handle lists bound inheritance; ActiveProcesses gives native tree accounting.

## Source-code evidence

Research date: **2026-09-23**.

### OpenAI Codex

`openai/codex@27969c0ae9c1ec23e359ff5133b4c36a8dd5b1ac`

Inspected:
- `codex-rs/core/src/spawn.rs`
- `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/win/job.rs`
- `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/win/conpty.rs`
- `codex-rs/utils/pty/src/win/psuedocon_tests.rs`

Classification: **OPEN_IMPLEMENTED** for inspected spawn/Job/ConPTY paths.

Current code provides KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE Job ownership, suspended-spawn + assign-before-resume, native process-handle termination, and current ConPTY tests for output closure/descendant/termination behavior. A separate compatibility helper may resume after assignment failure; CAP explicitly does **not** copy that fallback for its consequence-bearing path.

Lesson: **ADAPT_MECHANIC / REFERENCE_ONLY**. Do not import Codex planning/session authority.

### Goose

`aaif-goose/goose@201837dffc92ac3cce7ce7c3b3bb8fe4153dcc4b`

Inspected:
- `crates/goose/src/subprocess.rs`
- `crates/goose/tests/subprocess_cleanup.rs`

Classification: **OPEN_IMPLEMENTED** for inspected Linux owner-death mechanics.

Goose uses process groups plus `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` with parent identity recheck. Direct tests prove child death after true parent-process death and prove a long-lived child does not accidentally bind its lifetime to a temporary spawning thread.

Lesson: **ADAPT_MECHANIC / REFERENCE_ONLY**. CAP must test real owner death, not merely call `Child::kill()`.

## Failure lessons from current implementations / reports

- **Orphaned Windows descendants are a real operational failure class.** Recent Codex issue reports (#21994, #34614, #35726) describe parent/session termination paths that left grandchildren alive where Job containment was absent or not applied to that spawn path. These are issue reports, not independent proof of every root-cause claim, but they reinforce testing the exact owner-death path rather than assuming one shared helper protects all spawns.
- **Job containment and daemon detachment conflict by design.** Codex issue #44503 reports daemon startup being blocked by host Job semantics on one Windows environment. Native Host v1 therefore stays short-lived/owned and does not combine 'must die with owner' with daemon-detachment behavior.
- **PTY teardown is timing-sensitive.** Current Codex Windows PTY tests explicitly exercise descendant survival and termination; issue reports such as #14679/#25272 show teardown/AttachConsole failures in adjacent node-pty paths. CAP separates PTY from the first process slice rather than treating it as a trivial wrapper.
- **Lossy asynchronous output queues can corrupt evidence.** Codex issue #45540 reports multi-megabyte Windows output losing bytes when a broadcast consumer lagged. Native Host uses bounded backpressure and explicit output-limit failure; it must never silently discard output and still report normal completion.
- **Compiler provenance is consequence-relevant.** Rust 1.98.1 fixes a 1.98.0 rustc vtable miscompilation. Release evidence therefore pins an exact reviewed patch toolchain rather than mutable `stable`.

These lessons are used as failure hypotheses and test requirements; they do not make external projects part of CAP's trust boundary.

## Fit to this architecture

The selected design consumes the Core-v1 seam instead of creating another framework: Core owns why/when an effect is allowed and how ambiguity is reconciled; Native Host owns only the OS lifecycle needed to execute one already-authorized effect. Provider/native receipt remains evidence, and fresh project observation still determines verification.

The first slice intentionally excludes interactive PTY and sandbox policy because both add authority/security semantics beyond process ownership. That is narrowing the implementation goal, not weakening the final product boundary.

## Alternatives

### A — keep native lifecycle scattered in Python/Node/PowerShell

No new toolchain, but Job/native handle/strict inheritance/later ConPTY ownership remains split across higher-level runtimes and capability glue. **Not selected for the Native Host role**; those runtimes remain valid above the boundary.

### B — long-lived Rust daemon over named pipe/HTTP

Adds endpoint ACL/auth, daemon upgrade/version skew, reconnect, multi-client concurrency and pressure for durable host state/generic dispatch. **REJECT for v1**.

### C — one-operation Rust child over framed stdio

No discoverable endpoint, no durable host state, one attempt per lifetime, small provenance surface, natural Job/native-handle ownership. **SELECT / NARROW**.

### D — revive historical Rust-first CAP

Would replace/duplicate accepted Core, WorkingState, semantic projection and policy roles. **REJECT**.

## Minimum sufficient first implementation slice

After Core freeze only:

```text
one exact-version Rust binary
one versioned bounded stdio protocol
one active operation per host
Windows non-interactive process execution only
Job Object containment
suspended -> assign -> resume
native handle ownership
bounded stdout/stderr evidence
whole-tree hard cancel
owner-EOF cleanup
no PTY input
no sandbox
no daemon
no host durable state
no new Chat tool
```

ConPTY interactive input/resize, graceful interrupt policy, restricted-token/AppContainer sandboxing, persistent host sessions, cross-platform parity, generic Local Execution and host-side durable queues are **outside this first-slice goal** and require their own later slice/re-entry where they introduce new authority/security primitives.

## NativeHostProtocolV1 — frozen candidate contract

This is the exact first-slice protocol contract to implement **after Core freeze**. It is intentionally private and capability-adapter-facing; it is not a new public Chat schema.

### Transport framing

```text
frame := u32_be payload_length
         payload_length bytes UTF-8 JSON
```

Rules:

- zero-length frames are invalid;
- hard frame ceiling: **262,144 bytes** encoded JSON;
- no newline-delimited fallback and no concatenated unframed JSON;
- unknown `protocol_version`, message `type`, enum value or required field is fail-closed;
- stdout is protocol-only; host diagnostics use stderr and must never contain child stdout/stderr;
- child output is carried only as protocol `output_chunk` events;
- parent must drain host stdout and stderr concurrently while the host is alive.

### Hard v1 bounds

| Item | Bound |
|---|---:|
| protocol frame | 262,144 encoded bytes |
| identifier (`request_id`, `logical_operation_id`, `attempt_id`, refs) | 128 ASCII chars |
| executable path / cwd | <= 32,767 UTF-16 code units each after Windows conversion |
| argv count | 256 |
| one argv element | 8,192 UTF-8 bytes |
| encoded Windows command line | <= 30,000 UTF-16 code units |
| environment entries | 256 |
| environment name | 128 chars |
| one environment value | 8,192 UTF-8 bytes |
| total serialized environment values | 65,536 UTF-8 bytes |
| one raw output chunk | 32,768 bytes before base64 |
| operation output budget | caller-required, 0..8,388,608 raw bytes combined stdout+stderr |
| operation runtime budget | caller-required, 1..3,600,000 ms |

These are host hard ceilings, not grants. A capability adapter may authorize a much smaller scope/budget; Native Host cannot increase it.

### Handshake and messages

Host writes exactly one first message:

```text
HostHello {
  type = "host_hello"
  protocol_version = 1
  host_instance_id
  build_id
  target = "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc" | reviewed supported target
}
```

`host_instance_id` is fresh per process and has no durable authority. `build_id` is provenance evidence only; the parent independently verifies the installed binary identity before launch.

Parent may then send exactly one:

```text
BeginOperation {
  type = "begin_operation"
  protocol_version = 1
  request_id
  logical_operation_id
  attempt_id
  authorization_ref
  native_operation_ref
  executable
  argv[]
  cwd
  env { name: value }
  max_runtime_ms
  max_output_bytes
  containment_required = true
}
```

`authorization_ref` and `native_operation_ref` are opaque correlation values produced by the CAP adapter/Core path. Native Host echoes them but **does not interpret, issue, refresh or widen authorization**.

After Begin, parent may send only:

```text
CancelOperation {
  type = "cancel_operation"
  protocol_version = 1
  request_id
  attempt_id
}
```

Any second Begin, mismatched request/attempt identity or additional command family is a protocol violation and cannot create another target process.

### Host event stream

Events share:

```text
{
  protocol_version = 1
  host_instance_id
  request_id
  logical_operation_id
  attempt_id
  authorization_ref
  native_operation_ref
  event_seq
  type
  ...
}
```

`event_seq` starts at 1 after Begin and increases by exactly one. It is transport ordering/correlation evidence, not a project transition sequence.

Allowed operation events:

```text
operation_prepared
process_spawned
output_chunk
root_exited
operation_terminal
```

`operation_prepared` means request/bounds were accepted and required native containment resources are configured, but **no target has become runnable yet**.

`process_spawned` is emitted only after the suspended target is successfully assigned to the required Job and resumed. From that point onward, an external consequence may have happened; loss of later acknowledgement cannot authorize replay.

`output_chunk` contains:

```text
stream = "stdout" | "stderr"
stream_seq
encoding = "base64"
data
raw_len
```

Per-stream `stream_seq` is contiguous. The host never silently skips a chunk. If output exceeds the authorized budget, the host terminates the Job and emits an explicit terminal `output_limit_exceeded` outcome if the protocol channel is still available.

`root_exited` is non-terminal. It carries the root process exit code when known but cannot prove the descendant tree is empty.

Exactly one `operation_terminal` is emitted on a healthy protocol path, with:

```text
delivery_state =
    "never_runnable"
  | "tree_exited"
  | "terminated"
  | "host_failure_after_start"

reason = reviewed finite enum
root_exit_code = integer | null
target_ever_runnable = boolean
tree_quiescent = boolean
stdout_bytes / stderr_bytes
stdout_sha256 / stderr_sha256
output_complete = boolean
```

Interpretation:

- `never_runnable`: Host can prove the target never became runnable; this is delivery evidence only and does not itself authorize a retry;
- `tree_exited`: target became runnable and the Job is freshly observed quiescent;
- `terminated`: host intentionally terminated the Job because of cancel/timeout/output bound/owner shutdown; prior external effects may still exist;
- `host_failure_after_start`: target became runnable but the host could not produce the normal lifecycle guarantee/receipt; Core must treat consequence status conservatively.

The host **never emits `PASS`, `DONE`, `CONFIRMED_APPLIED`, `CONFIRMED_NOT_APPLIED` or `STILL_UNKNOWN`**. Those remain project Core/verification/reconciliation vocabulary.

### Host state machine

```text
START
 -> HELLO_SENT
 -> READY
 -> PREPARING
 -> PREPARED
 -> RUNNING
 -> DRAINING
 -> TERMINAL
 -> EXIT
```

Permitted shortcuts:

- `READY/PREPARING/PREPARED -> TERMINAL(never_runnable)` on validation/native setup/cancel failure before resume;
- `RUNNING/DRAINING -> TERMINAL(terminated)` after successful whole-Job termination;
- `RUNNING/DRAINING -> TERMINAL(host_failure_after_start)` when the host can still report a failure but cannot claim a clean natural/intentional terminal lifecycle.

Once `process_spawned` has been emitted or the target has actually been resumed, the host can never transition back to a `never_runnable` claim.

### Owner loss and process exit semantics

- EOF on host stdin is owner loss at every non-terminal state;
- before target resume: cleanup and exit without making target runnable;
- after target resume: terminate the Job/tree, reap/close native handles, then exit;
- no attempt is made to reconnect or find another parent;
- the host process exit code describes **host/protocol health only**, never target success;
- a normal host exit may accompany a child exit code of zero or non-zero;
- if a reliable terminal event was emitted and flushed, host exits 0; an internal failure that prevents reliable terminal reporting exits non-zero.

### Output integrity

The adapter reconstructs each stream from contiguous chunks and verifies terminal byte counts + SHA-256. Missing sequence, digest mismatch, `output_complete=false` or transport loss makes output evidence incomplete. Native Host may backpressure; it may not silently drop bytes and return a normal complete receipt.

### Explicit protocol non-features

V1 has no shell command string, PTY input, resize, stdin streaming to the child, upload/download, filesystem API, network API, daemon attach/resume, host persistence, host-side retry, host-side authorization lookup, plugin discovery or generic tool dispatch.

## Failure / crash matrix

| Failure boundary | Required behavior | Extra spawn before reconciliation |
|---|---|---:|
| binary/hash/protocol mismatch | unavailable/reject before target | 0 |
| malformed/partial/oversized frame | fail closed; no target | 0 |
| duplicate Begin | reject before second create | 0 |
| Job creation/config failure | fail closed | 0 |
| target created suspended; Job assignment fails | terminate/reap before resume | 0 runnable targets |
| assigned; host crash before resume | Job close cleans contained target; missing receipt remains conservative | 0 additional |
| resumed; Spawned ACK lost | Core `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`; no replay | 0 additional |
| host crash with active tree | Job close kills tree; Core reconciles external effects | 0 additional |
| parent/adapter dies | stdio EOF -> host kills Job/tree and exits | 0 additional |
| root exits while descendant remains | do not call tree complete; observe Job active-process state | 0 |
| cancel races exit | one terminal host state | 0 |
| nested-Job assignment incompatibility | fail closed; no uncontained resume | 0 runnable targets |
| PID reused | retained native handle governs ownership | 0 |
| protocol/Job handle inherited by target | qualification failure; implementation must structurally prevent | 0 |
| host restart after unresolved attempt | never replay old attempt automatically | 0 |
| Core says CONFIRMED_APPLIED / STILL_UNKNOWN | no respawn | 0 |
| Core says CONFIRMED_NOT_APPLIED | new attempt still needs fresh normal authorization | one separately authorized attempt |
| compiler/binary provenance moves | acceptance/review stale | 0 |
| machine/power loss | outside first-slice process-lifetime guarantee; Core fails closed/reconciles | 0 |

No release-critical cell in the selected first-slice process-lifetime scope permits blind re-spawn.

## Failure shields / acceptance ladder

### L1 protocol/state machine
- strict version + enum + size bounds;
- exactly one Begin;
- duplicate cannot spawn;
- stdout protocol-only;
- no raw shell command surface;
- host receipt cannot directly map to project PASS/DONE.

### L2 Windows lifecycle
- prove Job exists/configured before runnable child;
- assignment failure leaves no runnable target;
- child + grandchild die on cancel;
- hard parent death -> EOF -> host + descendants gone;
- exact handle inheritance allowlist;
- root-exit + surviving descendant is not falsely terminal;
- cancel/completion race has one terminal host state;
- identity-sensitive operations retain process handles.

### L2 CAP ambiguity integration
- inject crash after resume/before receipt;
- record unresolved/UNKNOWN;
- restart performs zero replay;
- CONFIRMED_APPLIED and STILL_UNKNOWN never respawn;
- CONFIRMED_NOT_APPLIED still requires a newly authorized attempt.

### Supply-chain / provenance
- exact Rust toolchain;
- committed Cargo.lock;
- dependency license/security checks;
- exact built/installed host hash in runtime receipt;
- source/runtime provenance in release-critical evidence.

### Review / physical
Production implementation requires hosted Windows CI/security, mandatory fresh ordinary-Chat exact BASE..HEAD semantic review, then target-Windows process-tree/owner-loss physical qualification on the reviewed head. Ordinary-Chat L3 is required only when a concrete Chat-facing capability consumes this host.

## Complexity budget

Adds only: one Rust binary, one private protocol/state machine, one Windows lifecycle module and one capability-adapter binding.

Explicitly avoids: RPC framework, service manager, listener, database/WAL, provider registry, scheduler/event bus, new public tool, second authorization system, second verifier, second WorkingState.

## Falsifiers / mandatory re-entry

Re-enter Stage Research if one-operation stdio cannot provide owner-loss semantics; a durable host-side replay/dedup store becomes necessary; first consumer requires interactive PTY or AppContainer/restricted-token sandboxing; nested-Job behavior prevents fail-closed contained spawn on supported Windows; or implementation creates a generic command runner reachable through existing public tools.

## First implementation blueprint after Core freeze

### Crate layout

Create a **new** crate on the accepted Core head rather than reviving the historical workspace:

```text
crates/native-host/
  Cargo.toml
  src/
    main.rs              # process entry; stdio handshake only
    protocol.rs          # framed messages, bounds, closed enums
    state.rs             # one-operation lifecycle state machine
    output.rs            # chunking, byte counts, SHA-256, backpressure
    error.rs             # finite host/protocol error taxonomy
    platform/
      mod.rs
      windows/
        mod.rs
        handles.rs       # OwnedHandle wrappers / close discipline
        pipes.rs         # child stdout/stderr pipes + inheritance list
        job.rs           # Job Object configuration/query/termination
        process.rs       # suspended CreateProcessW -> assign -> resume
  tests/
    protocol_contract.rs
    windows_process_tree.rs
    windows_owner_loss.rs
    windows_output.rs
    windows_races.rs
```

Keep Core adapter code outside this crate. The crate has no dependency on CAP policy documents, project configuration, WorkingState storage or semantic-projection code.

### Windows API map

| Host need | Win32 primitive | v1 rule |
|---|---|---|
| Job lifetime | `CreateJobObjectW` | unnamed private Job owned only by host |
| kill tree on final owner close | `SetInformationJobObject(JobObjectExtendedLimitInformation)` + `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` | required; no `BREAKAWAY` flag |
| create target non-runnable | `CreateProcessW` + `CREATE_SUSPENDED` | required before Job assignment |
| exact child handles only | `STARTUPINFOEXW`, `InitializeProcThreadAttributeList`, `UpdateProcThreadAttribute(PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST)`, `DeleteProcThreadAttributeList` | whitelist only child stdio handles; `bInheritHandles=TRUE` only with the explicit list |
| child stdout/stderr pipes | `CreatePipe` plus inherited child write handles / non-inherited host read handles | protocol handles and Job handle are never in child list |
| bind process to tree | `AssignProcessToJobObject` | failure before resume is fail-closed |
| make target runnable | `ResumeThread` on the primary thread returned by `CreateProcessW` | use documented primary-thread handle; do not require `NtResumeProcess` |
| root exit observation | `WaitForSingleObject`, `GetExitCodeProcess` | root exit is non-terminal tree evidence |
| tree quiescence | `QueryInformationJobObject(JobObjectBasicAccountingInformation)` | terminal natural completion requires `ActiveProcesses == 0` plus output drain |
| hard cancel / timeout / overflow / owner-loss | `TerminateJobObject` | whole-tree safety action |
| handle lifetime | `CloseHandle` behind RAII `OwnedHandle` wrappers | no raw handle lifetime in protocol/business logic |

`CreateProcessW` command line has a documented 32,767-character ceiling including the terminating NUL, so the protocol uses a lower 30,000 UTF-16-unit hard ceiling for the encoded command line. The executable path is passed separately as `lpApplicationName`, avoiding executable-name parsing ambiguity.

Windows handle-list inheritance explicitly requires inheritable handles and `bInheritHandles=TRUE`; this is safe only because the STARTUPINFOEX list is the allowlist. A structural test must prove the host's own protocol/Job/process handles are absent from that list.

### Internal concurrency shape

V1 needs concurrency only to avoid coupling child-output flow to lifecycle control:

```text
stdin/control reader
       |
       v
supervisor/state owner ---- Job/process handles
       |
       +---- stdout reader --\
       +---- stderr reader ----> bounded non-lossy event queue -> protocol writer
```

Rules:

- the **supervisor is the sole lifecycle state owner**;
- output readers cannot spawn/cancel/retry;
- protocol writer cannot change lifecycle state;
- queue capacity is bounded and backpressure propagates to child pipes;
- timeout/cancel/owner-loss supervision must remain able to terminate the Job even when output delivery is backpressured;
- no detached background task survives host exit.

Implementation may use scoped threads or a small async runtime, but adding Tokio is **not** a default decision. Prefer standard-library threads/channels unless implementation evidence shows they cannot satisfy cancellation and pipe-drain requirements.

### Error taxonomy boundary

Native Host errors are delivery/lifecycle facts, not retry policy:

```text
PROTOCOL_REJECTED
INVALID_BOUNDS
JOB_CREATE_FAILED
PROCESS_CREATE_FAILED
JOB_ASSIGN_FAILED
PROCESS_RESUME_FAILED
OUTPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
RUNTIME_TIMEOUT
CANCELLED
OWNER_LOST
OUTPUT_INTEGRITY_FAILED
HOST_INTERNAL_FAILURE
```

No error has a host-owned `safe_to_retry=true` field. Retry permission belongs to Core after reconciliation.

## Windows fault-test and helper blueprint

The first implementation must land with its fault harness. The harness is not a second runtime and is never installed with CAP.

### `native-host-test-helper`

Add a separate **test-only** binary crate:

```text
crates/native-host-test-helper/
  Cargo.toml           # publish = false
  src/main.rs
```

Release/install packaging must explicitly exclude this binary. No semantic tool, capability adapter or production config may resolve or invoke it. Its only purpose is deterministic subprocess behavior for hosted/physical Native Host tests.

The helper should use the Rust standard library wherever practical and expose a small closed CLI:

```text
native-host-test-helper exit
  --code <i32>

native-host-test-helper marker-sleep
  --marker <path>
  --sleep-ms <u64>

native-host-test-helper tree
  --pid-file <path>
  --root-exit-after-ms <u64|never>
  --child-ms <u64>
  --grandchild-ms <u64>

native-host-test-helper burst-output
  --stdout-bytes <u64>
  --stderr-bytes <u64>
  --pattern-seed <u64>

native-host-test-helper infinite-output
  --stream <stdout|stderr|both>
  --chunk-bytes <u32>

native-host-test-helper probe-handle
  --raw-handle <usize>
  --result-file <path>

native-host-test-helper wait-file-exit
  --ready-file <path>
  --go-file <path>
  --code <i32>
```

Helper behavior requirements:

- `marker-sleep` writes the marker as the **first user-code action**, so its absence proves the target never became runnable;
- `tree` records root/child/grandchild PIDs atomically enough for test observation, but PIDs are test evidence only and never Native Host ownership authority;
- `burst-output` emits deterministic binary bytes, not UTF-8-only text, independently to stdout and stderr so digest/ordering tests cover arbitrary process output;
- `probe-handle` calls the minimal Windows handle-query primitive and records `valid | invalid`; the host test deliberately passes the numeric value of an inheritable sentinel handle that is **not** in the child allowlist;
- `wait-file-exit` gives race tests a deterministic readiness barrier without adding a production synchronization protocol;
- helper modes never interpret CAP grants, environment policy or WorkingState.

### Fault injection mechanism

Use **two different layers**, because neither alone is sufficient:

1. **real Windows process tests** for Job/handles/tree/output/owner-loss behavior;
2. a **unit-only fake Win32 backend compiled under `cfg(test)`** for native call ordering and failures that are not safely/reliably inducible on a real runner.

The fake backend is not a production feature flag, environment variable or hidden runtime mode. Release builds must contain no fault-injection switch. Its API surface is just enough to record/fail the sequence:

```text
create_job
configure_job
create_process_suspended
assign_process_to_job
resume_primary_thread
query_job
terminate_job
close_handle
```

This proves `resume` is impossible after failed `assign` and lets tests force `PROCESS_CREATE_FAILED`, `JOB_ASSIGN_FAILED` and `PROCESS_RESUME_FAILED` without relying on machine-specific accidents.

### L1 protocol/state tests — platform independent

| Test | Injection | Required invariant |
|---|---|---|
| hello_is_first_and_single | normal startup | exactly one `host_hello` before parent command |
| zero_length_frame_rejected | frame length 0 | no Begin accepted; no target |
| oversized_frame_rejected_before_allocate | length > 262144 | bounded failure; no target |
| truncated_frame_rejected | EOF mid-payload | protocol failure; no target |
| invalid_utf8_rejected | non-UTF-8 JSON bytes | no target |
| malformed_json_rejected | invalid JSON | no target |
| unknown_protocol_version_rejected | version 2 | no target |
| unknown_message_type_rejected | foreign type | no target |
| unknown_enum_rejected | foreign enum value | fail closed |
| required_field_missing_rejected | omit attempt_id etc. | no target |
| identifier_bounds_enforced | 129-char id | no target |
| argv_env_runtime_output_bounds_enforced | each boundary ±1 | exact hard ceilings |
| duplicate_begin_cannot_spawn | send valid Begin twice | at most one spawn |
| cancel_identity_mismatch_rejected | wrong request/attempt | cannot affect owned operation |
| event_seq_contiguous | normal event stream | starts at 1, increments exactly 1 |
| stream_seq_independent_and_contiguous | stdout+stderr interleave | no gaps/duplicates per stream |
| terminal_event_exactly_once | all terminal paths | one terminal event only |

| host_error_has_no_retry_authority | every host error | no `safe_to_retry`/retry grant |

### L1 native ordering tests — fake backend

| Test | Forced failure/interleaving | Required call trace |
|---|---|---|
| job_create_failure | create_job fails | no create_process, no resume |
| job_config_failure | configure_job fails | no create_process |
| process_create_failure | suspended create fails | Job cleaned; no assign/resume |
| assignment_failure_never_resumes | assign fails | `create_suspended -> assign(fail) -> terminate/reap`; zero resume calls |
| resume_failure_is_not_spawned | resume fails | cleanup; no `process_spawned` claim |
| cancel_before_resume | cancel at PREPARED | cleanup; zero resume calls |
| owner_loss_before_resume | stdin EOF at PREPARED | cleanup; zero resume calls |
| cancel_after_resume | cancel at RUNNING | `terminate_job` exactly once despite duplicate cancel |
| timeout_cancel_race | timeout and cancel same tick | one termination owner / one terminal state |
| natural_exit_cancel_race | tree quiescence races cancel | one terminal event; never two contradictory outcomes |
| cleanup_is_idempotent | repeat internal cleanup | handles closed at most once / no use-after-close |

### L2 real Windows process-tree tests

| Test | Helper mode | Required evidence |
|---|---|---|
| basic_zero_exit | `exit --code 0` | `process_spawned -> root_exited(0) -> tree_exited`; output complete |
| basic_nonzero_exit | `exit --code 37` | tree still completes normally; root exit code 37 is evidence, not host failure |
| marker_proves_runnable_boundary | `marker-sleep` | marker cannot exist before host reaches resume boundary |
| child_and_grandchild_in_job | `tree` | all descendants are accounted for by Job while alive |
| root_exit_not_tree_exit | root exits immediately, descendants remain | `root_exited` emitted, **no terminal tree_exited** until Job active count reaches 0 |
| cancel_kills_entire_tree | long `tree`, then Cancel | root/child/grandchild all terminate within bound; terminal `terminated/CANCELLED` |
| timeout_kills_entire_tree | long `tree`, short runtime budget | no survivor; `RUNTIME_TIMEOUT` |
| host_stdin_eof_kills_tree | after `process_spawned`, close parent write end | host terminates Job/tree and exits; no descendant survives |
| hard_parent_process_death | external harness kills adapter process, not host | host observes owner pipe closure and cleans tree; proves real owner-death chain |
| host_process_kill_uses_job_close | externally kill host after spawned | KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE removes descendants even though host cannot emit terminal receipt |
| executable_not_found_never_runnable | missing exe | no marker/spawn; terminal `never_runnable/PROCESS_CREATE_FAILED` where reportable |
| invalid_cwd_never_runnable | missing cwd | no target becomes runnable |
| environment_round_trip | bounded unicode/env helper | exact environment received without inherited unrelated variables selected by test |
| command_line_boundary | args near 30k UTF-16 units | accepted at bound, rejected above; arguments arrive exact at helper |
| binary_stdout_stderr_integrity | deterministic binary burst | reconstructed bytes and SHA-256 exactly match helper expectation |
| simultaneous_stdout_stderr | burst both streams | no cross-stream corruption or deadlock |
| slow_parent_backpressure_no_loss | parent deliberately drains host events slowly, output under budget | exact bytes/digests preserved; host stays cancellable |
| output_budget_exceeded | `infinite-output`, small budget | Job terminated; explicit `OUTPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`; `output_complete=false` |
| child_closes_stdout_early | helper closes stream then remains alive | stream EOF is not tree completion |
| inherited_handle_allowlist | `probe-handle` with inheritable sentinel omitted from list | helper reports sentinel invalid |
| intended_stdio_handles_work | helper writes both streams | only intended child stdio handles function |
| protocol_handles_not_inherited | hold protocol pipe sentinel/open-state probe | target cannot keep host protocol alive accidentally |
| repeated_short_runs | 100 sequential hosts | no orphan processes/handles; no cross-run state |

### L2 transport ambiguity tests using real boundaries

These specifically prove CAP-style ambiguity rather than inventing a host retry mechanism:

| Test | Fault | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| transport_loss_before_begin | parent closes pipes after hello | no target |
| transport_loss_after_prepared_before_resume | close stdin at PREPARED | zero runnable target |
| result_channel_loss_after_prepared | parent closes host-stdout read end after PREPARED | host must not reinterpret broken output as permission to relaunch; if it resumes before detecting loss, Job cleanup applies and parent result is ambiguous |
| parent_loses_spawned_ack | drop/ignore `process_spawned` then terminate host/transport | physical target may have run once; zero automatic second spawn |
| host_crash_after_start_before_terminal | externally terminate host | descendants die by Job close; adapter/Core side records unresolved rather than fabricating success/failure |
| host_restarted_after_unresolved | start a new host process with no Begin | previous attempt is not reconstructed/replayed by host |

The exact Core `CONFIRMED_APPLIED / STILL_UNKNOWN / CONFIRMED_NOT_APPLIED` integration is tested later in the concrete consumer adapter because Native Host itself does not own those states.

### L2 race tests

Use `wait-file-exit` to create controlled interleavings. Each race runs enough repetitions to catch state-machine mistakes but has **outcome-set assertions**, not timing guesses:

- cancel vs natural root exit: either `tree_exited` or `terminated` may win, but exactly one terminal event and zero survivors;
- timeout vs natural exit: same single-terminal invariant;
- owner EOF vs explicit Cancel: at most one Job termination effect and no survivor;
- stdout EOF vs root exit vs descendant exit: terminal only after both output accounting is complete and Job is quiescent;
- duplicate Cancel frames: idempotent lifecycle effect; no second physical action;
- output-limit termination vs parent Cancel: one terminal state, output never reported complete.

No test passes merely because it slept an arbitrary fixed interval. Readiness is established by protocol events, helper marker files or native wait/query state, with an outer timeout only as a deadlock guard.

### Hosted CI versus physical Windows

**Hosted `windows-latest` is mandatory for every implementation head** for:

- protocol/state tests;
- fake-backend ordering/failure tests;
- normal Job containment;
- descendant cleanup/cancel/timeout;
- output integrity/backpressure;
- handle allowlist;
- owner EOF/hard adapter death where runner policy permits;
- race suite and repeated short-run leak/orphan checks.

**Target-Windows physical qualification remains mandatory before accepting the release-critical Native Host path** for:

- exact installed binary/source/toolchain provenance;
- normal contained launch on the supported user environment;
- child+grandchild cancel and owner-death cleanup;
- host hard-kill / KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE behavior;
- handle inheritance proof;
- sustained high-output/backpressure case;
- at least one crash-after-start ambiguity case proving no automatic replay;
- regression under the actual CAP launcher/adapter once a concrete consumer exists.

Hosted CI success never substitutes for the physical gate, but the physical gate should not be burdened with protocol-parser cases already deterministically covered at L1/L2.

### Leak/orphan acceptance rule

Every real-process test captures a before/after ownership snapshot scoped to the test run. On completion/failure it must clean up and assert:

```text
no helper root process remains
no helper child/grandchild remains
no Native Host child remains
no test-owned Job/process/thread/pipe handle remains live in the test process
```

A failed assertion must dump PIDs, host event trace, Job active-process observations and helper PID-file contents before cleanup so orphan failures are diagnosable instead of merely timing out.

### Test evidence artifacts

For physical qualification retain only bounded, non-secret evidence:

```text
native_host_build_id
Rust toolchain exact version
Cargo.lock digest
host binary SHA-256
repository HEAD
test case id
host event trace with payload data omitted/redacted where needed
process-tree PID observations
terminal receipt
orphan/leak result
```

Do not retain child stdout/stderr content by default; record byte counts/digests unless the specific fixture is synthetic and needed for debugging.

### Complete historical source inventory disposition

All source modules under the historical two Rust crates are accounted for:

- **ADAPT selectively:** `error.rs`, `contracts.rs`, narrow subprocess construction/testing ideas from `reaper.rs`, Cargo/lint/supply-chain patterns;
- **REJECT as Native Host owners:** `artifact.rs`, `audio_analysis.rs`, `audit.rs`, `binding.rs`, `bootstrap.rs`, `capability.rs`, `config.rs`, `confirmation.rs`, `input_capture.rs`, `job.rs`, `job_ops.rs`, `mastering_workflow.rs`, `media.rs`, `media_ops.rs`, `policy.rs`, `reaper_ops.rs`, `reference_mastering.rs`, `secret.rs`, `service.rs`; these are capability/state/policy/artifact/application concerns above or beside the new systems boundary;
- **REJECT old transport/runtime shape:** `transport/http.rs`, `transport/lifecycle.rs`, `transport/mod.rs`, `transport/protocol.rs`; only failure-test ideas survive;
- **REJECT entire historical relay-server role:** `crates/relay-server/src/{lib.rs,main.rs,model.rs,store.rs}`; its Axum/TCP/token/SQLite/lease/task ownership is unrelated to the private one-operation Native Host.

This inventory is intentionally asymmetric: most old Rust code is good historical project code but belongs to roles that the current architecture has since reassigned. `REJECT FOR HOST` means **wrong ownership boundary**, not "bad code".

### Salvage implementation rule

Do **not** cherry-pick the historical Rust crate or merge `chat/rust-relay-server` into the Core chain. When implementation opens, create a new minimal `native-host` crate on the accepted Core head and selectively port only reviewed mechanics whose owner/boundary still matches this table.

Expected dependency direction is intentionally small:

```text
serde / serde_json
thiserror (or equivalent small typed error layer)
sha2
windows-sys on Windows
+ only dependencies proven necessary by implementation/tests
```

Clap, chrono, jsonschema, keyring, HTTP, atomic-write-file and durable storage are **not default Native Host dependencies**. Add any of them only if the concrete first-slice implementation proves a requirement that cannot be met more simply.

### Unsafe boundary

The historical workspace forbade all unsafe Rust. Native Host cannot honestly keep that rule for direct Win32 lifecycle calls. The re-entry rule is narrower:

```text
safe protocol/state/output logic
 -> one platform/windows native module
    -> minimal reviewed unsafe blocks around exact Win32 calls
```

Unsafe must not appear in Core-facing protocol/business logic. Each unsafe block must have a local safety comment tying handle ownership, validity and lifetime assumptions to the wrapper invariant; hosted Windows tests exercise the wrapper behavior rather than treating compilation as proof.
